key_insight: Charge-density supervision improved atomistic energy prediction on QM9, but its benefits depended on the dataset.
engineering_relevance: Learning energy alongside spatial electron density could improve atomistic models while providing electronic information relevant to materials analysis.
method: Jointly predict energy and valence electron density from equivariant atomic graphs.
Integrate density-supervised real-space probe representations into the global energy regressor.
Analyze attention weights to identify influential probe locations.
evidence_signal: CDGNN reduced QM9 energy errors for interpolation and extrapolation to larger molecules, matched the baseline on small H-containing Fe and Fe-C datasets, and accurately predicted density distributions.
watch_item: Energy improvements were not universal; deployment requires charge-density training targets and validation on the intended material system.
paper_title: Charge density-supervised real-space representations for atomistic energy prediction
